transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started with our pre-publication check-in for 'Glass Harbor.' As you know, the catalog draft currently lists the film at 94 minutes with its premiere status still marked for confirmation. I need our submissions and technical screening staff to report any status or master-file issues before I make the final programming and delivery decision. What are we seeing on your end?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a premiere status issue. I checked the national festival database yesterday and confirmed that 'Glass Harbor' already had a public screening at the Coastline Film Week in this country. I recorded the result in my local review notes, but the database export feeding Mara's catalog review has not refreshed, so the catalog still shows premiere status as 'for confirmation.' Since national-competition entries must be national premieres, this film would not be eligible for the national competition based on what I found.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a master-file issue. This morning I completed ingest quality control and confirmed that the filmmaker's approved festival cut is an 88-minute DCP, not the 94 minutes listed in the catalog draft. The QC report is currently waiting in the technical queue and has not yet been attached to the programming record, so the catalog hasn't been updated to reflect the correct runtime.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Update the catalog draft to reflect the correct runtime of 88 minutes and the confirmed premiere status as 'not a national premiere' based on the Coastline Film Week screening.
Assign 'Glass Harbor' to the panorama program, as it is not eligible for the national competition due to its prior national screening.
Use the approved 88-minute festival cut DCP as the screening master for all panorama screenings.
Ensure the QC report and premiere-status findings are attached to the programming record before publication.
